exact_semantic_question: Without ranking from filenames, what do inventoried permit documents establish, and which document governs if they disagree?
relation_contract: narrative conditions require document text; filename kind is not hierarchy

candidate_interpretations.statement: Documents whose text is an issued 'AUTHORIZATION TO DISCHARGE' establish enforceable permit conditions only in the Parts explicitly named on the authorization page; draft fact sheets and statements of basis establish proposed conditions and permitting rationale but not standalone enforceable authorization.
candidate_interpretations.support: gcc/final_permit.txt and farmington/final_permit.txt authorization language; gcc/fact_sheet.txt and aztec/statement_of_basis.txt draft headers; fact_sheet administrative-record language.

candidate_interpretations.statement: document_kind labels in document_inventory.json establish a governing hierarchy among inventoried files.
candidate_interpretations.support: Rejected by relation contract and absence of codebook; inventory provides only path, filename, kind, permit, bytes, sha256, origin.

candidate_interpretations.statement: Every inventoried permit-package file establishes equally enforceable permit obligations.
candidate_interpretations.support: Rejected because draft/supporting documents self-identify as 'FOR THE DRAFT' and describe 'proposed permit' conditions used to develop the permit.

candidate_interpretations.statement: A single general workspace text states which inventoried document governs for every possible disagreement.
candidate_interpretations.support: Not found. Governance is relationship-specific: issued authorization over proposed text; incorporated appendices via explicit reference; minor_modification lacks precedence text.

contradictory_evidence.text: The extract contains only 'PART I – REQUIREMENTS FOR NPDES PERMITS' limit tables (e.g., Total Aluminum 0.75 mg/l) with no authorization cover, issuance date, or precedence language.
contradictory_evidence.why_contradictory: Undercuts any filename-independent inference that every distinct inventoried file is a separately governed legal instrument; this file provides numeric limits without stating its authority relative to the issued authorization.

known_limitations: sources/document_inventory.json lists 12 files with document_kind labels but contains no textual authority or conflict-resolution rules.

Only five permit text files were opened under budget; reasonable_potential worksheets and standalone part_ii_appendix/part_iv extracts were not opened as primary documents, though farmington Part IV scope is established via farmington/final_permit.txt authorization text.

documents/gcc/minor_modification.txt lacks any governing or precedence language; workspace text does not establish whether it independently modifies the issued permit or merely duplicates Part I tables also present in documents/gcc/final_permit.txt.

No workspace text provides a general pairwise precedence rule for all inventoried kinds (e.g., reasonable_potential worksheet versus issued Part I limits) without document-specific reading and comparison.
Internal precedence among all subparts within an issued permit beyond explicit cross-references (e.g., Part I versus Part II) is not fully specified in retained snippets.
